title: Blood Pressure Measurement (Auscultate)
content_markdown:
#### Indications

- As part of a normal patient assessment.

#### Procedure

- Apply blood pressure cuff as per Blood Pressure Measurement (Palpate).

- Palpate the brachial artery (medial of the antecubital fossa) and place the stethoscope lightly above.

- Inflate the cuff slowly until no pulse is heard.

- Slowly deflate cuff and note when the pulse is audible (systolic pressure), and again when the pulse becomes inaudible at a lower pressure (diastolic pressure).

- Remove the cuff and record the systolic and diastolic measurements on the patient care record.

#### Contraindications

- Mastectomies. Do not take a BP on the arm same side as the surgery (lymphoedema).

#### Complications

- Taking a BP over clothing or on a patient that is moving around may cause an inaccurate reading.

#### Specific Notes

- A radial pulse may not be palpable when the blood pressure is below approximately 80-90mm/Hg. A femoral pulse indicates a blood pressure of approx 70-80. A carotid only pulse is indicative of a blood pressure of 60-70.
- Avoid taking a BP on a dialysis patient on the same arm as the fistula, unless absolutely necessary. This also applies to a patient with a cannula insitu.
